enforced_by: DETERMINED (not deferred), 2026-09-03 audit, escalation #1384: this rule governs Claude's real-time conversational/tool-use conduct within a turn -- there is no durable code or DB artifact a configmaint.validate scan could check after the fact to confirm or refute compliance. Mechanical enforcement does not apply to this class of rule; the realistic enforcement path is direct researcher review of transcripts/sessions, not automation. If this determination is wrong for this specific rule, flag it -- not left open as a default.

rule_text: Any module that a researcher or Claude operates by hand -- not purely internal library code called only by other code -- has a dedicated PS entry point under `governance.scripts_ps_dir` (`iba/app/ps/`). A module reachable only via raw Python or raw SQL is a usability and audit gap, found live 2026-08-18 against this very system: 3 build cycles of `cfg_behaviour_class`/`cfg_behaviour_rule` before `Behaviour.ps1` existed.

rule_text: A change to a tool, module, or user-facing behaviour is not complete until `USER-GUIDE.md` reflects it, in the same unit of work -- `governance.User_Guide_scope` states what the guide must cover ("the latest state of all the tools"); this rule states when it's updated. Found violated live 2026-08-18: 3 build cycles of the operational-behaviour system (escalation #715) had zero `USER-GUIDE.md` coverage before this rule existed.
source: researcher, 2026-08-18 (escalation #732); governance.User_Guide_scope; same shape as governance.build_md_on_code_change for BUILD.md

Corrected framing from this session's own earlier read: this is not primarily a same-commit-timing correlation rule (the git-heuristic idea from #1384's first pass is dropped) -- it is a standing discipline that the guide is kept current whenever a tool/module/user-facing behaviour changes, full stop. rule_text: Every active PS script under `governance.scripts_ps_dir` (`iba/app/ps/`) that performs a real project operation dispatches through `run.py` (`python -m iba.app.run <package> --step <step> --run-id <id>`) -- not a direct call into the underlying Python module. Dispatching through run.py is what gives an operation a real `run` row, a `run_id`, `cfg_step` registration, and `module_blocking` protection; a script that calls its module directly leaves no record anywhere that it ran, when, or with what result -- not a partial record, none (escalation #8, checked live 2026-08-20: 8 of 45 scripts bypassed run.py this way). Two named exceptions, both permanent and architectural, not violations: (1) `Start-Iba.ps1` -- necessarily, since it bootstraps what run.py itself depends on; (2) `Escalation.ps1`'s `-Action Raise/Update/AnswerRun` -- a deliberate manual front door onto the escalation system's own backlog workflow, not a pipeline run (its `-Action List/History` DO dispatch through run.py, work package `escalation-reporting`, fixed this session per D4/D16/D23). Any other bypass is real non-compliance, not a third exception -- tracked as its own escalation, not silently accepted.
enforced_by: BUILT 2026-09-03, escalation #1384: cfgquality.find_ps_scripts_bypassing_runpy() (scans iba/app/ps/*.ps1, exempting Start-Iba.ps1/Escalation.ps1, for direct iba.app.handlers/lib/tools calls with no iba.app.run dispatch in the same file), wired into configmaint.validate + CONFIG-REPORT.md. Verified live: 1 found (Behaviour.ps1 -- matches the known non-compliance this rule's own text already named 2026-08-21, confirmed still true, not fixed here, now re-detected every run instead of relying on a stale note).

rule_text: When building or validating anything -- code, config, or process -- a point that requires a NEW decision (a judgement call, an ambiguity, something not already specified) is TERMINAL: it must not be answered inline and resumed. It is recorded as an open item and routed back into design/specification; work resumes only after the design is settled and approved. A point that instead reveals Claude's own execution error against an ALREADY-settled, already-approved design (a typo, a wrong parameter, a slip) is SELF-CORRECTABLE: Claude fixes it directly, records what was wrong and what changed, and continues -- no new approval is required, because no new decision was made. The distinguishing question is always: does resolving this require deciding something new, or only correcting execution against something already decided? A recurring decision_required outcome on the same routine, run after run, is itself a defect -- it means a threshold or parameter that should have been specified once, in config, during design, was left to be re-asked every time instead. That is a design gap to close (add the missing config), not a pattern to formalise.
enforced_by: escalation.resolution_kind (decision_required | self_correctable) for escalation-raised items -- see cfg_enum 'resolution_kind' and cfg_escalation_requirement.

rule_text: AnswerRun's flat approve/reject/revise/hold/noted vocabulary is refused for BOTH resolution_kind values -- unreachable for any dispatcher-tied escalation raised under the resolution_kind regime. decision_required must be answered through Update's richer vocabulary (ready_for_approval -> approved; -State on-hold; next_action=reject/revise/noted) -- checked and confirmed live before this half existed (escalation #820): AnswerRun silently accepted a flat 'approve' on a decision_required item, collapsing the record of a genuine judgement call into the same one-line outcome a self_correctable item gets. self_correctable must be closed via resolve-self-correctable, or converted via escalate-to-decision -- this was always the APPROVED spec (escalation-decision-vs-defect-axis-proposal-v4-20260822.md §6: 'No approve/reject/revise/hold/noted vocabulary. AnswerRun is never invoked' -- and its own §11 Stage 2 test named this exact check), never actually built or tested during #799's Stage 2 -- confirmed live the same way (escalation #822): a flat 'approve' succeeded with no refusal at all. Net effect: neither kind ever had a genuine use for AnswerRun's original 'answer and resume the same run' semantics -- decision_required runs terminate and never resume (a fresh run is the test, §5); self_correctable never carried decision vocabulary to begin with (§6).
source: researcher, 2026-08-22, escalation #795, on decision_required: "I suggest to check and test the answer to the question in the configs, my expectation is that it should not be possible and that the configs should now state that." The self_correctable half was already in the approved proposal (v4 §6/§11 Stage 2) but never built or tested in #799 -- found checking the first half, not separately instructed.
enforced_by: iba/app/lib/escalation.py answer_for_run() -- refuses at the top of the function if esc_row['resolution_kind'] is 'decision_required' OR 'self_correctable' (i.e. always, since resolution_kind is required at every Raise). The mirror-image guard, update()'s own dispatcher carve-out (refuses UNLESS resolution_kind='decision_required'), already existed from #798/#799 and is unchanged.

rule_text: Each module or utility, from now on (case-by-case as it comes up in development, NOT retrofitted to existing modules), must have a test plan. The test plan covers every meaningfully different interaction, parameter, and option combination of that module/utility's intended functionality -- not a single happy-path example. The test plan is a living artifact: when a functional component changes, the test plan for that component is updated in the same unit of work, before the change is considered complete -- the same 'same unit of work' discipline governance.build_md_on_code_change already applies to BUILD.md. The test plan is RUN after the design is approved and the build (per the approved plan) is complete -- a required stage inside the existing plan/propose/design (in detail) -> approve -> build per the plan -> approve cycle, not a separate optional step. The test results are included IN the build's escalation resolution when requesting final approval -- not just claimed as 'tested live' in prose without the actual per-case results shown, and not omitted. Origin: escalation #795, where the approved proposal's own named Stage 2 test ('self_correctable has no reachable AnswerRun path') was written into the design document but never actually run before the build was reported complete -- twice, once for each half of the same function. A written-but-unexecuted test is indistinguishable from no test at all.
source: researcher, 2026-08-22, verbatim: "I think we got to the stage where we need to have a re-usable test pack for all development tasks... each module or utility in future must have a test plan. the test plan must include testing all the different interations, params options of each of the module/utility intended functionality. this test plan must be updated to include modifying the testing plan for each functional component after a change. the test plan must then run through after the design, and the results of the test must be included in the resolution of the build... however, the test plan method will be introduced case by case as further development takes place, rather than trying to develop test plans for all modules."
enforced_by: No automated check yet -- deliberately, per the researcher's case-by-case rollout instruction (building a configmaint.validate check now, before any real test plan exists to check against, would be exactly the 'machinery-heavy design' simple-steps-not-engineered-designs warns against). Practical enforcement today is manual: the next module/utility design proposal should name its test plan as part of the design, and the build's resolution should carry the test plan's actual results. A configmaint.validate check (e.g. 'every active cfg_utility/cfg_work_package has an associated test plan reference') is a natural candidate to add once the first real test plan exists and its storage convention (table vs doc) is chosen against that real case -- not designed speculatively here.

The covered table's own current row already holds current content exactly once; duplicating it into the log is a defect, not a safety margin. payload is NULL for insert events and for one-time migration-baseline rows, where no prior state exists.

rule_text: A filename uses lowercase, hyphens (not underscores/spaces), a compact YYYYMMDD date where a date is part of the name, a -v{n} version suffix with no leading zero, and zero-padded numeric ids where an id is part of the name.

rule_text: A snapshot (a report, an extract, a point-in-time analysis) gets filename versioning: -v{n}-{date}, same-day revisions bump {n}, prior versions archived promptly, only the latest stays at the live path. A living document (a guide, an instruction doc meant to be edited in place) keeps one stable filename, with its version tracked in its own metadata and git history, never archived copies.
enforced_by: not_mechanically_checkable, 2026-09-03 audit: classifying a given document as 'snapshot' vs 'living' is itself a judgement call this rule exists to guide, not a fact a scan could verify independently.

rule_text: A superseded snapshot is archived (moved to the folder's archive/ subfolder, never deleted) in the same unit of work that supersedes it -- findable again via the manifest, not left live alongside its replacement.
enforced_by: partially_enforced, 2026-09-03 audit -- VERIFIED: reportkit.write_report()'s own archive-on-write (archive_before_write/_archive_prior_versions, iba/app/lib/reportkit.py) mechanically archives every superseded report on write, confirmed live this session (escalation history/list reports auto-archived correctly). Does NOT cover hand-authored deliverable docs written outside reportkit (design docs, catalogue docs) -- archiving those (e.g. yesterday's characteristic-tables-cross-db-inventory-v1 -> v2 supersession) is still manual discipline, unchecked.

rule_text: Before writing a new file: determine its correct folder first (don't default to the working directory); archive any file it supersedes; never leave a file sitting at a folder's root when a subfolder convention exists for its type; follow the naming-shape and snapshot-vs-living rules above without being asked each time; and confirm the destination when genuinely unclear rather than guessing (docs/interaction-preferences.md's own protocol).
enforced_by: not_mechanically_checkable, 2026-09-03 audit: this is the umbrella filing-discipline rule (determine correct folder, archive supersessions, confirm when unclear) -- each concrete sub-behaviour it describes is covered by its own more specific rule (naming-shape, snapshot-vs-living-document, archiving-trigger) which each carry their own enforcement_status; this umbrella rule itself has no separate checkable artifact beyond those.

rule_text: A tool's own auto-generated report output (an escalation list/history export, CONFIG-REPORT.md, a validation run's report, a content-index rebuild report -- anything a *.report_path/*.output_dir cfg_setting names) stays exactly where that setting points. An AUTHORED deliverable document (a plan, a design doc, a gap analysis, an investigation write-up) that is produced FOR one specific escalation's work belongs under outputs/escalation/, not iba/docs/ -- the researcher's own confirmed intent (escalation #971 chat, verbatim: "yes the refiling of escalation files is for 976"). iba/docs/ is for engineering/planning documentation that is NOT tied to one specific escalation (architecture notes, cross-cutting design references). That contradiction was plausibly a real contributing cause of this project's own escalation-tied-document filing drift (dozens of files landed in iba/docs/ following the clearer, but wrong, first sentence). Migrating the EXISTING iba/docs/ backlog into outputs/escalation/ is still escalation #976's scoped-migration job, not silently done by this rewrite -- this only fixes the rule text and governs new documents going forward.

rule_text: If a table, column, or row is marked inactive in the configs (cfg_table.inactive / cfg_column.inactive / an active=0/inactive=1/delete_flagged=1 row), it is never included in any report, analysis, or result -- unless the request explicitly asks to explore historical/inactive data. Simplified 2026-09-03 per researcher correction: repeatedly going back over inactive/historical data to rebuild or reconcile it, unprompted, is itself a violation of this rule's intent, not a form of thoroughness -- it wastes time and produces confusing results. Default to ignoring inactive state entirely; only engage with it on an explicit historical-exploration ask.

rule_text: An escalation item sitting at next_action_assigned_to=Claude in an open working state (review/in-progress) has exactly two legitimate outcomes each time Claude touches it -- never a third, silent option of leaving it as-is with no comment: (1) COMPLETE the work and move it forward (typically to ready_for_approval, handing the actual decision to the Researcher), or (2) if not complete or if Claude is genuinely UNSURE how to proceed, write a comment stating the status/question and reassign it to the Researcher (next_action_assigned_to=Researcher) -- do not leave it silently assigned to Claude hoping to return to it later. The same applies to an item Claude finds itself unsure whether to apply even after approval (state=approved, e.g. a genuine ambiguity like a superseding note contradicting the approval): reset it via Correction to next_action=ready_for_approval, assigned_to=Researcher, with the conflict stated plainly -- an approved item assigned to Claude that the Researcher cannot act on through the normal Update path is a dead end for both parties, not a safe resting state.

enforced_by: partially mechanical: the Stop hook (.claude/hooks/stop_check_escalation_backlog.py, escalation-operational-friction-review-v1-20260831.md Addendum 4) surfaces every open Claude-assigned item every turn -- this rule states what Claude must actually DO about what it surfaces, not just acknowledge it. No structural DB-level guard yet (deliberately -- a hard block here risks the same overreach as the removed actor_must_be_assignee, escalation #1346); this is the record of the standing instruction the hook exists to make un-ignorable.

rule_text: An escalation-tied working file (a design doc, scope/reconciliation doc, checklist, worked example, or similar authored deliverable produced to progress one specific escalation's work -- in Workflow/Catalogue/, iba/docs/, or an equivalent authored-deliverable folder) carries that escalation's numeric id as its filename prefix ('{id}-{descriptive-name}...'), matching the pattern already established for the auto-generated '{id}-escalation-history.md' report (escalation #857) -- extended here from that one report type to every escalation-tied authored document. Does NOT apply to living/standing documents (GOVERNANCE.md, CHARTER.md, USER-GUIDE.md, BUILD.md, slash-command definitions under .claude/commands/) or to reusable scripts (which follow the CLAUDE.md section-6 _check_/_apply_/etc. behavioural-prefix convention instead) -- only escalation-scoped authored deliverables.
